How do urban scenes shape brain signals?

EEG distinguishes early visual responses from later appraisal of green urban scenes.

Our everyday environments are designed. What can this published study actually tell us about their relationship with human health and the brain?

The study

Researchers recorded brain responses to images of natural and built features in urban environments and compared visual characteristics with subjective judgments.

The findings

Greener scenes elicited more positive ratings and distinct event-related EEG components, including P1, N1 and later appraisal signals. These are momentary processing markers, not evidence of permanent structural change.

What this means for architecture

Design decisions influence what people see and how scenes are appraised, suggesting hypotheses for real-world urban experiments.

Conclusion

The evidence points to an important research question, not a universal design rule. Better controlled and longer-term studies are needed.

Brain and Environment study (2026)
